lesson.menu_title: The Question Behind the Question — Listening Under Pressure
lesson.menu_desc: Decoding a long question, buying three seconds, and answering the thing that was actually asked -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- The Question Behind the Question
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernando Meneghelli Bottura | Lesson 3 -- Listening Under Pressure
lesson.grammar_point: modal perfects for speculation and self-assessment

listenings.text: Here is the thing candidates almost never work out, and it costs them the room. When a panel asks a long question, the length is not the question. The length is context, and the question is usually the last eight or nine words. People start answering the context, because that is the part they understood first, and by the time they reach the end they have answered something nobody asked. So train one habit. Do not listen for words, listen for the verb at the end. Tell me, walk me through, how do you decide, what would you do. That verb is the instruction, and everything before it is scenery. And if you did not catch the verb, you say so. Sorry, could you repeat the last part? That is not a weakness, and I have never once written it down as one. What I do write down is when somebody answers confidently and completely off target, because that tells me they will do the same thing in a board meeting.

Right, so, before we go into the detail of the transformation, and I appreciate a lot of this is public anyway, I want to understand something about the way you operate rather than the outcome, because the outcome we can read. You had a group of nine entities, three of them loss making at the point you arrived, and a board that had already announced a target externally. What I would like you to talk me through is not what you cut. It is how you decided the order. What went first, what you deliberately left until last, and why.

extra_audio.text: Anneke asks a long question and Fernando does not catch the last part. Fernando asks her to bear with him and to repeat the final part. Anneke repeats the instruction, which is to talk her through the order of his decisions. Fernando paraphrases the question back to her to check that he has the gist. Anneke confirms and Fernando answers the question that was actually asked.
